purpose: Bounded ANES 2016–2020–2024 panel route from pre-election financial worry through federal-government trust and post-election reported vote, preserving identity, attribution, remedy, and later action limits.

events.geography: United States; 2016–2020–2024 ANES Panel Merged Study subset
events.date_precision: 2024 pre-election panel wave anchor; exact respondent interview dates are not retained
events.denominator: 2,154 valid weighted observations for worry × federal trust and 1,699 for pre-election worry × post-election reported presidential vote; panel subset, not full 2024 cross-section
events.method: Official ANES 2024 Full Release SDA weighted descriptive cross-tabs using the 2016–2020–2024 panel subset and complex-design standard errors
events.missingness: No dated bill, price, employer, household shock, responsible actor, alternative, remedy, recovery, later institutional response, or validated vote record is retained
events.exposure: Respondents reported pre-election financial worry ranging from not at all to extremely worried
events.alternatives_before_action: Household financial alternatives, adaptation, borrowing, support, and non-use are not observed in the panel cross-tabs
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Financial worry is a subjective material-pressure signal; the underlying price, bill, income change, or household consequence is not identified
events.choice_or_response: Pre-election worry is compared with federal-government trust and post-election reported presidential vote; the cross-tabs do not identify the respondent's political reasoning or attribution
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Respondents report worry and vote; parties, candidates, media, prior identity, and institutions may shape interpretation, but no actor-level episode is retained
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: No remedy or institutional response to a dated material event is observed
events.immediate_outcome: The panel supplies a temporally ordered descriptive material-attitude-action surface
events.protected_outcome: Political judgment or vote choice may provide a channel for expressing material concern; no policy or material protection is observed
events.sacrificed_outcome: Household financial burden, unmet need, and any practical sacrifice are not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: No transfer of cost, risk, information, or power can be assigned from the cross-tabs
events.later_outcome: No later policy response, trust persistence, household recovery, switching, political organizing, or exit is observed
events.meaning_and_attribution: Federal-government trust and reported vote provide institutional and political meaning surfaces, but prior party identity and information remain major alternative explanations
events.public_or_collective_response: Reported vote is observed after the pre-election worry measure; turnout, contact, organizing, policy response, and collective action are not linked
events.counterexample: The relationship is non-monotonic in trust and can reflect identity persistence or political interpretation rather than a direct material-to-vote mechanism
events.source_and_uncertainty: Official ANES SDA descriptive panel cross-tabs; panel retention, self-report, confounding, and lack of a direct material event prevent causal interpretation

arrows.evidence: The panel cross-tab places pre-election worry and pre-election federal-government trust in the same retained panel subset; the extremely worried group has 70.3% in some/never trust versus 51.9% among the not-at-all worried group
arrows.counterexample: The pattern is non-monotonic and can reflect prior party identity, information, retrospective judgment, or selection into the retained panel
arrows.remaining_gap: Dated material event, prior trust/identity, actor attribution, and later trust persistence

arrows.evidence: The panel cross-tab places pre-election worry before post-election reported vote; the extremely worried group reports 55.4% Trump and 36.9% Harris, while the not-at-all worried group reports 32.0% Trump and 66.5% Harris
arrows.counterexample: Worry is not a direct bill or hardship event, vote is self-reported, and prior identity, candidate preference, and information can explain both measures
arrows.remaining_gap: Dated household exposure, alternatives, attribution, turnout validation, policy response, and later material outcome

arrows.to: policy response, collective action, recovery, or exit
arrows.evidence: The retained ANES layer ends at trust and reported vote and contains no linked remedy, policy response, recovery, organizing, switching, or exit outcome
arrows.counterexample: A vote or institutional judgment can express identity or candidate preference without producing a material policy response or later behavior
arrows.remaining_gap: Actor-attributed policy response, repeated judgment, collective action, household recovery, trust persistence, and exit

boundary: This ledger formalizes a temporally ordered ANES panel bridge from subjective financial worry to federal-government judgment and reported vote. It does not establish a dated material shock, causality, attribution, remedy, policy response, recovery, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only retained official SDA cross-tab estimates and source metadata are represented; the publisher's panel microdata are not locally reproduced in this artifact.
